messages:
carmen: Heads-up — the RBAC default-role backfill failed during the nightly run. psql job hit a unique constraint on role_slug when inserting default_role for several tenants. partial run left some rows in limbo. :grimacing:
ben: Ugh. Any error lines?
carmen: Error snippet from worker log:
```
ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "roles_slug_key"
DETAIL: Key (slug)=(default) already exists.
```
alice: Was that from the v2 backfill script (roles_backfill_v2)? we added a uniqueness assertion last week.
ben: That assertion is intended, but the backfill used INSERT not upsert. If the earlier run crashed mid-transaction we could have created partial state.
sec-oncall: Is this causing outages? audit logs look fine so far, but some admin flows hit 500s when resolving default role for orgs with partial rows.
carmen: Not an outage yet, a handful of orgs see permission resolve errors on app startup. We rolled the backfill to paused. deploy-bot: Backfill job "roles_backfill_v2" paused by carmen at 02:07 UTC.
datateam: We should do a deterministic reconciliation: convert the insert -> upsert with a WHERE NOT EXISTS or ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then re-run idempotently. But must be careful with role IDs shifting.
alice: Agreed. Also we have audit implications — we need to ensure each synthetic backfill action gets audit entries and uses the service account key so we can trace the change. auditor-bot: New audit entries will be created for backfill runs under service_account:rbac-backfill-runner.
ben: Two concerns: 1) existing orphan role_mappings referencing the old transient role IDs, and 2) KMS key rotation window yesterday might mean some older audit payloads couldn't be decrypted by the audit pipeline. Carmen, did you notice missing audit payloads?
carmen: Yes small number of decrypt errors in the pipeline logs around 23:49 UTC yesterday. I talked to infra — keys rotated but new consumer config missed one key alias. sec-oncall: KMS rotation was intentional; infra is reattaching aliases now. We need to avoid running destructive migrations until audit can decrypt prior entries in case we must rollback.
ben: Plan proposal:
1) Add idempotent upsert SQL for default role creation: ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name WHERE roles.slug IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.slug; (plus preserve existing id)
2) Run reconciliation in small canary batches (100 orgs) with extra tracing enabled.
3) Emit explicit audit events tagging run_id and service_account.
4) Verify KMS-decrypt of past 48h audit payloads before wider rollout.
5) Lock write path for role schema migration window (5m) and have quick rollback SQL ready.
alice: For orphan mappings, we should add a mapping-fix step after upsert: for any mapping where role_id is missing, map to the canonical default_role.id using slug lookup. Keep that in a separate transactional step so we can preview diffs.
sec-oncall: I'll create a short runbook checklist and coordinate a 10:30 UTC canary. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rbac-backfill (internal).
datateam: SQL preview snippet to test locally (please run in a sandbox first):
```sql
BEGIN;
-- create canonical default role if missing
INSERT INTO roles (slug, name, created_by)
VALUES ('default', 'Default Role', 'service:rbac-backfill')
ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name
RETURNING id;
-- repair mappings that reference missing role ids
UPDATE role_mappings rm
SET role_id = r.id
FROM roles r
WHERE r.slug = 'default' AND rm.role_id IS NULL;
COMMIT;
```
carmen: I'll run the canary after infra confirms KMS alias fix. Ben can you prepare the quick rollback SQL (delete rows created by run_id or mark them as tombstoned)?
ben: On it. I’ll also add a short query to detect duplicate slugs and collate affected org ids.
auditor-bot: Auditor: scheduled verification job queued. Will report once 48h decrypt checks pass.
sec-oncall: If canary looks good, we target 3:00 UTC full backfill with a 15-minute maintenance window and pager standby.
carmen: Thanks everyone. tagging @ben @alice for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
